t: Section 302(i) of the Federal Corrupt Practices Act, 1925 (2 U.S.C. 241 (i)) is amended by inserting immediately before the period at the end thereof a comma and the following: “and the District of Columbia”.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment that adds "and the District of Columbia" to a definition in the Federal Corrupt Practices Act. The tempting reading is that an election-related statute involves the public, but nothing here has the federal government consulting outside parties, holding hearings, making rules, or granting a right to sue. It only changes the geographic scope of a defined term.

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely technical amendment to a statute, extending its geographic scope to include the District of Columbia. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It simply changes the text of a law.
qwen_block.s: Section 302(i) of the Federal Corrupt Practices Act, 1925 (2 U.S.C. 241 (i)) is amended by inserting immediately before the period at the end thereof a comma and the following: “and the District of Columbia”.

opus.w: This is a technical amendment that adds the District of Columbia to an existing provision, most likely the definition of "State." It creates no process that lets people outside the federal government take part in a federal decision. Neither the mention of D.C. nor the election-law setting makes it participation, since elections are an explicit exclusion and no consultation, hearing, rulemaking or right to sue is created.
opus.s: is amended by inserting immediately before the period at the end thereof a comma and the following: “and the District of Columbia”
opus.b:
This is a "No."

**Tempting-but-wrong reading:** The section amends the Federal Corrupt Practices Act, which deals with elections, and it adds "the District of Columbia," a non-federal jurisdiction. That could look like bringing an outside entity into a federal process. It fails because the amendment only changes a definition. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. Elections are also listed as a trap under the definition.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple legislative amendment that expands the geographic scope of an existing act to include the District of Columbia. It does not establish any process for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties (such as DC residents, local government, or experts) before making a decision. There is no advisory committee, public hearing, comment period, or consultation requirement described in the text. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: Section 302(i) of the Federal Corrupt Practices Act, 1925 (2 U.S.C. 241 (i)) is amended by inserting immediately before the period at the end thereof a comma and the following: “and the District of Columbia”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending a law to include the District of Columbia implies some form of consultation or participation by DC residents or officials. However, the text itself is purely a legislative amendment to a statute's geographic scope. It does not describe any process where the federal government consults with outside parties (like DC residents or officials) before making a decision. It simply changes the definition of who is covered by the act. There is no advisory board, public comment period, consultation with states/tribes, or right to sue mentioned. The amendment is a unilateral legislative act.
